chain.g: unity, copper coin, the unit of coinage

ety.text: Inherited from Middle English as, from Old French as, from Latin as, assis (“unity, copper coin, the unit of coinage”), probably borrowed from Etruscan. Doublet of as.

senses.d: A playing card showing a single pip, typically the highest or lowest ranking card in a game.
A die face marked with a single dot, typically representing the number one.
The ball marked with the number 1 in pool and related games.

ex: […] maybe two or three twenties, a dozen tens, and twenty or thirty fins. The rest is all aces and silver.
If they got too many aces (dollar bills) or fives or tens, they turned them in to the vault where they became part of the reserve.

senses.d: A very small quantity or degree; a particle; an atom; a jot.
ex: He will not bate an ace of absolute certainty.
I'LL not wag an ace farther: The whole World ſhall not bribe me to it;

senses.d: A serve won without the opponent hitting the ball.
A point won by a single stroke, as in handball, rackets, etc.
The best pitcher on the team.
To pass (a test, interviews etc.) perfectly.
To defeat (others) in a contest; to outdo (others) in a competition.
To win a point against (an opponent) by an ace.
To make an ace (hole in one).

ex: Negativity toward asexuality can make emerging aces fear that something is wrong with them.

grp.label: single point or spot on a card or die
tennis, volleyball: point scored without the opponent hitting the ball
